title: When Allah's help and the opening arrive.
subtitle: Victory as a sign, not a trophy

key.label: What the elders heard / what Ibn Abbas heard

then: Ibn Abbas called this {idea}the last surah revealed{/idea}. When Umar asked the elders of Badr about it, some said it commands praise at victory. Young Ibn Abbas said it was {trap}Allah informing the Messenger ﷺ that his life was ending{/trap}. Umar agreed. The opening here is the conquest of Makkah.
now: You finally get the thing you worked for years for: the degree, the house, the job. The party is planned. {idea}This surah suggests a different reading of success{/idea}: it may be a sign that a chapter is closing, and a reminder to look toward your Lord.
old: Success means I have arrived and can relax.
new: Success is help from Allah and a sign my time is moving. I respond with Him in mind.
try: When something good happens today, say first: this is from the help of Allah.

title: You see people entering Allah's religion in crowds.
subtitle: Years of patience, then whole tribes at once
then: Ibn Kathir says the Arab regions {trap}were waiting for Makkah before accepting Islam{/trap}, saying if he wins over his people he is a true Prophet. After the conquest {reward}they entered in crowds{/reward}; within two years the peninsula was full of faith. Jabir later wept, remembering the Prophet ﷺ said they would also leave in crowds.
now: You have been patient for years with a child, a project, a family member who never comes to the masjid. Nothing moves. {reward}Then one day it all opens.{/reward} And Jabir's tears are a reminder: holding on matters as much as arriving.
old: If nothing has changed after all these years, nothing will.
new: Allah can open in a moment what years of effort seemed not to move. Then I hold on.
try: Make dua today for someone you have been patient with for a long time, by name.

title: At the peak, glorify Him and ask forgiveness.
subtitle: The response to victory is humility

row.title: praise and istighfar
sub: He did it, forgive my gaps

then: A'ishah said the Prophet ﷺ often said in his bowing and prostration: {idea}Glory to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me{/idea}, living out this verse. Near the end of his life he often said: {reward}glory and praise to Allah, I seek His forgiveness and repent to Him{/reward}.
now: At the top of your achievement, your mind says: I did this. The verse says: {idea}glorify, praise, ask forgiveness{/idea}. Even the best effort had gaps, and the help was His. Ending a good thing with istighfar is how the best of people ended.
old: Asking forgiveness is for when I have done something wrong.
new: Even at my best moments I glorify Allah and ask His forgiveness, as the Prophet ﷺ did.
try: Add this to your ruku and sujud today: Subhanaka Allahumma Rabbana wa bihamdika, Allahumma-ghfir li.
